risks: Low: rounds are part of care and follow existing prescribing responsibilities. Risks are stopping a medicine a resident still needs, and discussing end-of-life medicines without the resident or family.
consent: Rounds are care, not research: residents or substitute decision-makers are told about the rounds at admission and before their review, and may decline changes. The evaluation uses routine data under determination QA-2026-077, with no individual consent.
data: The informatics lead exports administration records with study numbers; the pharmacist links them to round notes on the operator's secure drive; reports show counts by home only.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: residents with dementia, residents without family, residents whose first language differs from staff, and short-stay residents may be reviewed less or have their wishes heard less. Reach and family participation are reported by length of stay and by whether a substitute decision-maker took part; interpreters are booked for reviews where needed.
effectiveness: Success is sustained rounds that reach most residents and lead to carried-out recommendations without more falls or restarts.
efficiency: About one hour of pharmacist, physician and nurse time per home per month, within approved time.
costs: Staff time within approved roles; no additional budget.
grants: None needed; results could support regional funding to extend the model.
partnerships: The operator's quality lead, the three directors of care, a family council representative from each home, and the informatics lead.
rebPath: The regional research ethics board determined the evaluation to be quality assurance using routine data, not requiring REB review (QA-2026-077, 2026-09-04); any publication will state this determination.
limitations: No comparison group; documentation-based fidelity; the study cannot show clinical benefit.
summary: Low-risk evaluation of routine care under a quality assurance determination, with equity reporting by length of stay and family participation.
